identity: Writer and university teacher · People's Republic of China · 1899–1966
title: Lao She's birth chart
metaDescription: Lao She's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.2° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a trine: the Sun and Pluto within 0.3°, identity wired to depth. A trine is an open channel. The two cooperate without being asked, which is exactly why it is easy to spend and easy to take for granted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 14.2° Aquarius: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mercury. A air sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 27.4° Capricorn, Venus at 27.6° Sagittarius, Mars at 23.2° Cancer. Mercury in a earth sign reads as a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; Venus in a fire sign reads as taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; Mars in a water sign reads as drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.3°. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, Saturn opposition Neptune at 1.2°, and Mercury opposition Mars at 4.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aquarius at 14.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Scorpio at 7.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Cancer at 23.2° is in fall. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 air, 3 water, 3 fire, 1 earth by element and 5 mutable, 3 fixed, 2 cardinal by mode. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. Mars, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 7.3°.
